title: "Functions"
format: html

Reusable helpers. Each takes its inputs as arguments and reads no global objects, and each is tested on synthetic data with a known answer in [`tests/test-functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/tests/test-functions.R).

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/functions.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/setup.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/functions.R")
```

## Yes/no fields

The CMS-2728 form records comorbidities and insurance as yes, no or unknown. A condition counts as present only when a field is "YES"; missing or unknown counts as not present. The original code returned missing for missing fields, which would drop patients from the models; the published sample sizes show the paper's models did not.

```{r}
#| label: fn-any-yes
#| eval: false
```

## Insurance

The original code's hierarchy, unchanged: no insurance, then Medicaid, then Medicare (including Medicare Advantage), then employer group, then other (including VA).

```{r}
#| label: fn-derive-insurance
#| eval: false
```

## Nephrology care

Combines whether the patient saw a nephrologist with how long. Unknown is its own level, so the models keep the patients the paper kept.

```{r}
#| label: fn-derive-nephrology-care
#| eval: false
```

## Census region

Regions by state name, because usRds labels the residence state with its name (format `$STATFIP`). This replaces the original code's state-label spreadsheet.

```{r}
#| label: fn-assign-region
#| eval: false
```

## Dartmouth codes

Sets Dartmouth's -88888 and -99999 to missing. The original code turned every negative value positive, which would have entered suppressed HSAs as 88,888 or 99,999.

```{r}
#| label: fn-clean-dartmouth-codes
#| eval: false
```

## Finding spreadsheet columns

Finds exactly one column for each measure, or stops and lists the candidates.

```{r}
#| label: fn-select-by-pattern
#| eval: false
```

## Spreadsheets with title rows

Dartmouth spreadsheets put titles above the header; this finds the header row.

```{r}
#| label: fn-read-header-table
```

## ZIP codes

Restores leading zeros that spreadsheets drop (for example 501 becomes 00501).

```{r}
#| label: fn-standardize-zip
#| eval: false
```

## Alternative columns

Takes, row by row, the first value present across several columns. A release of the Medical Evidence file has the provider ID as `PROVUSRD_DIAL` or as `PROVUSRD`, and this picks whichever is there.

```{r}
#| label: fn-first-non-missing
#| eval: false
```

## Unique keys

Stops if any key appears more than once, and otherwise passes the data on, so it can end a pipeline. Every lookup table is checked this way before it is joined to patients.

```{r}
#| label: fn-assert-unique
#| eval: false
```

## Checking ACS variables

Compares each year's ACS label with the expected pattern and stops on any mismatch or absent variable.

```{r}
#| label: fn-check-acs-labels
#| eval: false
```

## Density categories

Zero facilities is its own category; the other four are cut at the quartiles, each including its upper bound, as in the original code.

```{r}
#| label: fn-density-categories
#| eval: false
```

## eGFR limit

Applies the eGFR restriction: at or below the limit, or strictly below it, as set in `setup.R` (open decision #D2).

```{r}
#| label: fn-egfr-within-limit
#| eval: false
```

## Odds ratios

Extracts the density terms of a fitted model as odds ratios with Wald confidence intervals and the number of patients the model used.

```{r}
#| label: fn-density-odds-ratios
#| eval: false
```

Builds outcome ~ exposure + covariates + (1 | HSA) from names, so each model's covariates are a list in `setup.R`.

The share of the variance of eGFR at each level of a null mixed model.

## Classifying codes

Sends the codes to one provider in batches, through that provider's own function, and asks once more for any codes the model skipped.

```{r}
#| label: fn-classify-codes
#| eval: false
```

## Reading a JSON answer

Reads a model's plain-text answer that holds a JSON array, with or without a ```` ```json ```` fence around it. Used for Claude, which is asked for JSON text instead of ellmer's structured output.

```{r}
#| label: fn-parse-json-answer
#| eval: false
```

## Checking a provider's answers

Stops unless the model answered every code exactly once, invented no code, and used only the six category names.

```{r}
#| label: fn-check-votes
#| eval: false
```

## Saving each provider's answers

Saves a provider's checked answers the first time and reads them back on a rerun, so a failure in one provider never means paying the others again.

```{r}
#| label: fn-cached-votes
#| eval: false
```

## Combining the models

One row per code with each model's category; a code is accepted only when all three agree.

```{r}
#| label: fn-ensemble-agreement
#| eval: false
```

## HSA population

Builds the exposure's denominator from ZCTA populations, counting each ZCTA once per HSA and year even when several of the HSA's ZIP codes share it.
